The recommended dose of naratriptan in the UK is 2.5 mg, and in the USA it is 1 or 2.5 mg. If no response is obtained with the initial dose, a second dose should not be taken for the same attack. If symptoms recur af- ter an initial response, the dose may be repeated after an interval of 4 hours, to a maximum of 5 mg in any 24-hour period. For doses in hepatic or renal impair- ment see below. Administration in hepatic or renal impairment. Nar- atriptan is contra-indicated in patients with severe hepatic or se- vere renal impairment (creatinine clearance less than 15 mL/minute). In patients with mild to moderate hepatic or re- nal impairment, the recommended maximum dose in 24 hours is 2.5 mg and a lower starting dose should be considered. Migraine. For comparison of the relative benefits of different triptans in migraine, see under Sumatriptan, p.627. Further references. 1. Ashcroft DM, Millson D. Naratriptan for the treatment of acute migraine: meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. Phar- macoepidemiol Drug Safety 2004; 13: 73–82. Preparations USP 31: Naratriptan Tablets.
